subject: Rapid provisioning validation plan — NimblePay POC SLOs & scale behavior
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot@nimblepay.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Rapid provisioning validation plan — NimblePay POC SLOs & scale behavior

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the NimblePay platform team. Quick recap and a concrete validation plan so we can get you an accurate performance profile for the POC next week. Please confirm the items below or flag corrections.

Key SLOs you asked us to validate in the POC:
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 200 ms for single-request text-generation at 256 tokens (baseline model).
- Streaming: first-token p50 <= 80 ms, sustained streaming token latency p95 <= 40 ms.
- Throughput: sustained 600 requests/minute with 4 concurrent sessions per customer (target concurrency 480 active connections).
- Scale-up target: additional 1k concurrent sessions on demand within 45 seconds of spike detection.
- Degradation policy: queueing allowed, max queue time 8s before returning 429 with retry-after and automatic fallback to smaller model.

Proposed validation plan (timeline & responsibilities):
1) Today (Priyom): share SLO matrix + quick lab test config (attached: nimblepay-slo-matrix.xlsx).
2) Thu 07:00 PDT (Redwood infra team): run synthetic spike sim — step load to 1.5x target for 10 min, capture scale-up timing and queue lengths. (Owner: Karthik)
3) Thu 09:00 PDT (NimblePay devs): run representative traffic replay (Prod-like prompt mix). We'll coordinate runbook + corpus. (Owner: Elliot)
4) Thu 11:00 PDT (Joint): review traces, KV cache hit rates, streaming first-byte times, and priming behavior; decide warm-pool sizing. (Owners: Marissa + Sofia)

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Can NimblePay tolerate occasional p95 spikes up to 350 ms for under-1m windows during cold scale events?
- Is persistent connection keepalive acceptable for long-lived streaming sessions (we recommend 60s keepalive)?
- Are there hard limits for burst capacity billing/quotas we should be aware of?

Next steps: please reply to confirm the schedule above and attach a sample request corpus (10–20 prompts) for the replay. If you want a longer warm pool (we can keep instances prewarmed for up to 15 minutes), call that out.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Rapid provisioning validation plan — NimblePay POC SLOs & scale behavior

Thanks Priyom — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications:

1) Latency tolerance: we can accept p95 up to 300 ms during short cold-start windows (<= 90s), provided we have a clear retry/backoff guidance for clients.
2) Streaming behavior: streaming is critical for our checkout flow. First-token latency is highest priority; we want p50 first-token <= 100 ms to feel snappy for end users. Sustained token p95 <= 50 ms is acceptable.
3) Concurrency profile: our peak active sessions are expected ~700 for the US region during promos; 1k is a nice-to-have but 800 sustained is the real target.
4) Billing/quotas: we have a negotiated burst allowance with infra that caps per-minute spikes to 2x baseline unless we prebook burst capacity. We will surface that in the replay corpora.

I attached a tiny sample corpus (10 prompts) — can you confirm the exact headers we should use for the replay (auth, client-id, model-id)? Also, we prefer graceful queueing over immediate 429s for the checkout path, up to your 8s cap.

Thanks,
Elliot

--
Elliot Barnes

Subject: Re: Rapid provisioning validation plan — NimblePay POC SLOs & scale behavior

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Elliot — good note on the streaming first-byte target and the 800 sustained concurrency expectation. Operational commitments from Redwood for this POC: 

- Warm pool strategy: we recommend keeping a small warm pool sized to ~15% of expected sustained concurrency (120 instances) with automatic replenishment. For NimblePay we will test both 120 and 240 warm sizes to see cold-start reduction. Warm instances maintained for up to 10 minutes between spikes.
- Scale orchestration: when queue depth exceeds 30 simultaneous requests or when CPU utilization > 70% for 30s, the autoscaler will spin additional workers. Measured target: add 300 concurrent-capacity units within 20–30s, beyond that add at 100 units per 15s. Aggregate goal: reach +1k concurrent capacity within 60s in our conservative estimate; optimistic path hits 1k within 35–45s if prewarmed pool is sufficient.
- Queueing policy: FIFO with priority tags for checkout traffic (tagged-high). Max queue time 8s; for checkout we will honor the 8s but attempt graceful partial responses for long polls. After 8s the API returns 429 with Retry-After and backend fallback to a low-cost model if configured.
- Streaming priming: to meet first-token p50 <= 100 ms, we will use persistent connections and a tiny prefix priming cache for the most common prompts; we expect p50 to drop below 90 ms for primed connections.

Planned tests for Thursday (owners assigned):
- Karthik: synthetic step ramp (infrastructure) — measure scale-up latency, cold-start percentiles, and queue durations.
- Priyom: traffic replay orchestration and logging hook setup (we'll need your client-ids and tokens).
- Neha: SLO runbook & alerting thresholds; will propose Slack alerts + automated HubSpot event on breach.

Deliverables after the test: 1) SLO verification report (latency/throughput traces), 2) recommended warm-pool config for production, 3) an ops runbook with retry guidance for NimblePay devs.

Could Elliot or Sofia confirm they can do the replay at 09:00 PDT and share a short-lived token for the run? If you want us to prewarm more aggressively we can — we'll log cost delta.

- Replay headers: Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>; x-client-id: nimblepay-web; x-model: rw-medium-v2; x-priority: checkout/high
- Monitoring hooks: we'll post metrics to the joint dashboard (link above) and stream traces to your SRE Slack channel. Keep an eye on KV-cache-hit and stream-first-byte metrics.
- Failure mode capture: please let us know if you want capture of raw request payloads (we can redact PII) — we'll include one export.
- Post-run meeting: 11:00 PDT standup for 30 minutes to review results and pick warm-pool sizing. Deliverable: perf report by 14:00 PDT with suggested production config and estimated incremental cost for prewarming.

Action items assigned: 
- Elliot: share sample tokens and the 10–20 prompt corpus by 08:00 PDT tomorrow.
